pre_mortem: Brown loses because frequent blitzing does not necessarily create productive checkdowns: CIN's -0.11 EPA/dropback against blitz could mean sacks, failed possessions or quick throws to Higgins and Chase instead. His aggregate yardage also does not reveal whether one play inflated the sample. Flowers loses because CIN's clearest defensive weakness is its 5.30 rushing YPC allowed; Henry's 65 recent carries offer BAL a credible way to control possession and avoid a pass-heavy chase. Neither leg is script-proof, and missing availability and weather checks prevent treating these as finalized wagers.
